cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: I hear the chest is light again. I do not hear things; I am told them, kindly, by people who owe me. My offer stands. My terms have not changed, which at this point is a kindness.

left.label: Borrow
left.outcome: Ten marks in, one in ten out, monthly. The bell on her door rings for you now.

right.label: Not from you
right.outcome: "From whom, then? I ask because I would like to buy their debt."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The chest cannot meet next watch's wages. For the record, the Company will advance them against the Keeper's own salary. For the record, that is not a kindness. It is a lien.

left.label: Take the advance
left.outcome: The hands are paid. You are not, for a season.

delayed_resources.message: The Company recovers its advance from the chest.

right.label: Pay them short and explain
right.outcome: Dace explains. Badly. The hands understand anyway, which is worse.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The hands drink on credit at my bar because you pay them late. I've carried it a month. I'm not a bank. I'm a reeve with a cellar. Who's paying, Keeper, you or the moot?

left.label: The Coffers, what there is
left.outcome: The chest empties into the inn. The hands are sober, briefly.

right.label: Cut the hands' credit
right.outcome: "Right. I'll tell them who said so."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: Sorry. I know there's no money. The west paddle needs a new spindle or it needs a prayer. I've asked Hale for the prayer. She says the spindle's more reliable. I agree with her. I never agree with her.

left.label: The spindle, somehow
left.outcome: You sell the good chair. Cole buys it back for less than she gave it.

right.label: The prayer
right.outcome: Hale prays over the paddle. It runs another month. Nobody explains it.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. Wages are two watches late. Two hands have gone down to Lock 6 where the Keeper pays. And the rest are asking me if I'm going too.

left.label: Sell the Company lamp oil
left.outcome: The town has oil for a month. Vosk will ask. Not yet.

right.label: Ask them to wait one more
right.outcome: "One more. Right. That's what I said last time."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Your chest is empty. Mine isn't. I'll pay a season's tolls in advance at face value, no discount, no conditions. I'm not being generous. I'm buying a Keeper who remembers who paid the wages.

left.label: Take the season
left.outcome: The chest is full of Sorrel coin. You remember.

delayed_resources.message: Sorrel barges pass on tolls paid in advance.

right.label: No Keeper is for sale
right.outcome: "Everyone's for sale. Some of you just haven't seen the price yet."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper, the Board has noticed the chest. The Board does not like noticing chests. There is a phrase in their letter, 'fiscal stewardship', which I have never seen used kindly.

left.label: Ask the Board for relief
left.outcome: Relief arrives: a loan at Company rates, and Vosk's closer attention.

right.label: Raise tolls until it recovers
right.outcome: Bargees pay more and say so. The chest breathes.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: The chest has a false bottom you did not know about. Under it, twenty marks in old coin and a note in Dray's hand: 'For the day the Company stops paying. It will.'

left.label: Take it; the day has come
left.outcome: Twenty marks. The note goes in the Ledger.

right.label: Leave it; the day is not yet
right.outcome: You close the false bottom. You know it is there now, which is something.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: You have missed a payment. I have sent no men; I said I would not. I have sent a note to the Company, as I said I would. Kindly expect a visitor.

left.label: Pay double now
left.outcome: The chest bleeds. The note is withdrawn, kindly.

right.label: Let the Company come
right.outcome: Vosk reads the note twice. "Noted. Irregular. Both of you."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The moot's had an idea. A town toll, on top of the Company's, for the town's own works. Collected at your gate, by your hands, into a chest that isn't yours. The Company would hate it.

left.label: Collect the town toll
left.outcome: Two chests on the sill. Bargees pay both, swearing. The town mends its roofs.

right.label: One toll, the Company's
right.outcome: "Thought so. Had to ask. The moot made me."

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You have sold Company property to meet wages. I know because I know. For the record, I have not written it down. For the record, I am deciding whether to.

left.label: Write it down
left.outcome: "Noted. You are the first to say that." She writes less than she could.

right.label: Ask her not to
right.outcome: "I did not hear that. You will find I hear very well."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: I've been paying for spindle oil myself. Roughly a mark a week. Sorry. I didn't want to add to the chest. I'm telling you now because I've run out too.

left.label: Pay her back, all of it
left.outcome: Six marks. She tries to refuse. She takes it.

right.label: Ask Tamm for tallow instead
right.outcome: Tallow. The gears run, greasy and slow. Quenn does not complain.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Two things. A bargee's offered to pay his toll in coal instead of coin, and the Company store'll take coal. And half the hands have no coal at home.

left.label: Coal to the hands
left.outcome: Warm houses, empty Book. Vosk notes a toll paid in 'kind'.

right.label: Coal to the store, coin to the chest
right.outcome: The store pays less than the toll was worth. The chest breathes anyway.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Delay costs, and so does poverty. I can put you in touch with a Sorrel banker who lends to Company posts against future tolls. It's legal. Barely. The Company would call it 'irregular'. The Company isn't broke.

left.label: Meet the banker
left.outcome: Sorrel gold in a Company chest. The paper is very long.

delayed_resources.message: The Sorrel banker's note comes due.

right.label: No Sorrel money
right.outcome: "Suit yourself. The Aldmere bankers won't call you either. They don't lend to canals."

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: Nothing in the chest but the chest. The hands know. The town knows. The Company will know on Tuesday. There is one thing left to sell, and it is the Keeper's own good name at the gate.

left.label: Sell precedence for a week
left.outcome: The queue reorders itself by coin. It is fast and ugly and pays the wages.

right.label: Go to the moot with empty hands
right.outcome: The town votes a levy on itself. For you. Nobody expected that.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The chest holds more than the toll table can produce. I have checked the table. I have checked the Book. For the record, one of them is wrong, and it is not the table.

left.label: Remit the surplus to Ardent
left.outcome: "Noted. Correct." The surplus goes east. The Book is honest again.

right.label: The Book is right
right.outcome: "Noted." She underlines something.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: A full chest attracts attention. I would not dream of lending to you now; I would like to borrow. A small sum, at your terms, for a building. It would be kind. It would also be recorded.

left.label: Lend to Cole
left.outcome: The Company's money in Cole's building. It is the most irregular thing you have done.

right.label: The chest is the Company's
right.outcome: "Of course. I only wanted to hear you say it."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Word is the chest is full and the town's roofs are not. The moot's asked me to ask: is any of it the town's, or is it all going to Ardent to buy a Board member a launch?

left.label: Fund the roofs
left.outcome: Slate on every roof in the low street by winter. Vosk reads the entry twice.

right.label: It goes to Ardent
right.outcome: "Right. I'll tell them. I'll tell them the word 'launch', too."

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: There's money. There's actually money. Sorry, I've never said that before. I could rebuild the west paddle gear properly. Both sides. Marrow's pattern. It would take the whole surplus and it would last fifty years.

left.label: Marrow's pattern; the whole surplus
left.outcome: Six weeks. The gear runs like water. Vosk approves the spend without a word, which is unheard of.

right.label: Keep the surplus for a bad year
right.outcome: "Right. Sensible. Sorry. I'll patch it."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: The chest is heavy. The hands know it's heavy because they carry it. And they've asked, politely, whether a heavy chest means a bonus or just a heavier chest.

left.label: A bonus
left.outcome: A mark a man. Ilse's takings double for a night.

right.label: A heavier chest
right.outcome: "Right. Just checking." They carry it anyway.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: You're rich. Relatively. My principals would like to buy the summit's surplus lamp oil, rope and tallow at a premium. The Company will say its stores aren't for sale. The Company isn't here. I am.

left.label: Sell the surplus stores
left.outcome: The chest grows. The stores shrink. Winter is a way off.

right.label: Company stores stay
right.outcome: "Fine. I'll buy them from Lock 8. Tobin sells anything."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper! The summit's accounts are the envy of the flight. The Board has asked how. I said 'the Meridian spirit'. They asked again. I would be grateful for a sentence I could send them.

left.label: Efficient tolling and dry weather
left.outcome: Pell sends it. Ardent accepts it. Vosk, reading the copy, does not.

right.label: Send them the Book
right.outcome: "The Book. Itself. Ah." He does not send it. He sends a summary.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: The chest will not close. Coin on coin, scrip on scrip, and no honest line in the Book that adds to it. Whatever you have been doing, you have been doing well. Someone will ask.

left.label: Bury half in the false bottom
left.outcome: Dray's hiding place holds. Nobody has ever looked. Yet.

right.label: Spend it on the town, visibly
right.outcome: A new wharf crane. The town cheers. The Book cannot explain the crane.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: A Board auditor from Ardent arrives Tuesday to count the chest against the Book. I would rather the count was right than that he found it wrong. For the record, this is not advice.

left.label: Make the Book right
left.outcome: Three nights of honest arithmetic. The count matches. He is faintly disappointed.

right.label: Let him find what he finds
right.outcome: He finds it. He is not disappointed. Vosk says nothing at all.

cards.speaker: cole
cards.text: The town says the Keeper is rich. The town says it the way it said it of Dray, the month before he went. I am not warning you. I am a landlady. I am telling you what tenants say.

left.label: Ask what they said of Dray
left.outcome: "That he'd found something worth more than tolls. Kindly forget I repeated it."

right.label: Let them talk
right.outcome: "They will. They do. I collect it, like rent."

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: Somebody tried the toll chest last night with a bar. My potboy saw them off. Sorrel accent, he says. A full chest is a lit lamp, Keeper. Either spend it or guard it. Right now you're doing neither.

left.label: Post a guard
left.outcome: Dace's man sleeps on the chest. It is very uncomfortable and very safe.

right.label: Spend it down on the gates
right.outcome: New timber, new gear, and a chest no thief would bother with.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: With this much in the chest I could hire a proper survey of the north bank. Sorrel engineers, not Company. I'd like to know what's under there. Sorry. I've wanted to know for six years.

left.label: Hire the survey
left.outcome: Sorrel engineers on the north bank for a week. Vosk watches them from the Company house.

right.label: The Company surveys its own bank
right.outcome: "It doesn't, though. That's rather the point. Sorry."

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. Vosk's counted the chest twice this week. Kell's coming. And the hands say if the Keeper's going to be arrested they'd like their bonus first.

left.label: Pay the bonus
left.outcome: Paid. The hands are loyal for a month, which is longer than most things.

right.label: Nobody is being arrested
right.outcome: "Right. I'll tell them that. They'll believe it about as much as I do."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: I know where the surplus came from. On my shore nobody minds. On the other they mind a great deal. My principals could buy a 'consultancy' from you, papered and legal. It costs a favor later.

left.label: The consultancy
left.outcome: Paper covers coin. The favor is not named. It will be.

right.label: Let it stand
right.outcome: "Brave. Or slow. I'll find out which when Kell does."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: Keeper, I have defended the summit's accounts to the Board with every adjective I possess. I am running out. Either the surplus goes to Ardent this week or I stop defending, and I have never stopped anything.

left.label: Send it to Ardent
left.outcome: The chest is honest and light. Pell finds new adjectives.

right.label: Stop defending
right.outcome: He stops. It is very quiet. Kell arrives on Tuesday.
